label: Greater Houston
appNote: For an install (clients.cjs market): stateName and timezone drive the app's labels and clock, stateBox the drawn-outline check, naip the aerial photo search (Planetary Computer: Texas 2022, flown 13-21 Sep 2022 over Houston; checked 2026-11-16). Houston's sources are bulk files, not query services, so they carry no url for the lot outline on the door map (the doors' own lot lines are in metros/out/<town>-lots.json).
note: Houston market (Matthew 2026-11-16: 'just sixfold but texas edition ... focus houston and surronding markets ... only lawn care and aeration'), to test with Bryce (aeration and seeding, Houston). Each county's appraisal district publishes its roll as bulk files; each file's terms were read before it was pulled (terms below). Every single-family home (state class A1) is a door; the homestead exemption marks whether the owner lives there (occ here / away). Data only: no install, client file or login yet.

lawn.check: 16 Nov 2026, 20 single-family lots in Pearland/Manvel (Brazoria file), pictures looked at: Colorado's green line (NDVI 0.33) read 0 lawn on 17 of 20 lots. In the Texas NAIP 2022 photo plainly green St. Augustine/Bermuda reads NDVI 0.10-0.25 and tree crowns under ~0.33 (the 2024 photo is from Oct-Nov 2024 and shows dormant Bermuda: not used first). Roofs and paving read below 0, bare ground 0.05-0.10. At 0.12 the lawns read 300-6,600 sq ft on 3,300-15,000 sq ft lots and match the pictures (front and back lawns counted, houses, drives and shrub beds left out). Known gap: the 2018 laser predates houses built since (fast-growing suburbs), so on those lots its tree crowns and roof can be stale; the photo still decides what is green.
lawn.note: Yard v2 lawn measuring (metros/yard-metro.mjs, V2 settings). Photos: NAIP Texas 2022 (13-21 Sep 2022, late summer by the classifier's rule) first, 2024 (10 Oct - 19 Nov 2024) second; the classifier uses the late-summer one. Laser: USGS 3DEP 2018 coastal surveys on the public Entwine bucket, depth 10 (1.4-1.6 m tiles, like Colorado's 1.2-1.8 m). No DRCOG (Denver only).

montgomery.why: The district's data is marked 'The Montgomery Central Appraisal District retains all rights to the data. Redistribution or commercial use of this data is prohibited without prior authorization from the Montgomery Central Appraisal District.' The fuller tax-parcel view (owner, homestead, year built) says 'Users must comply with Montgomery County's data access policies'. Traverse is commercial use, so this needs MCAD's written authorisation first. Nothing pulled.

waller.why: Not cheap: no bulk download found from the appraisal district itself (resellers and the state's StratMap layer only); not looked into further.
